meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'something, a thing or two' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I want to show you something.

examples.text: И ещё кое-что. Эдуард Владимирович просил передать привет.
examples.trans: And one more thing. Eduard Vladimirovich asked us to pass on his regards.

examples.text: Без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: Without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.
The partners discussed the terms of the deal in detail.

examples.text: Заодно без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: At the same time without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

examples.text: У нас с тобой серьёзный разговор.
examples.trans: You and I have a serious talk to have.

examples.text: Есть интересный разговор. Всё хорошо, малыш.
examples.trans: There's an interesting conversation. Everything is fine, kid.
We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!
I am not going to run away.
The dog is running away into the park.
I am not planning to run away anywhere.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

meanings.en: nowhere, not anywhere (direction/destination, used with не or нет)

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'stairs, staircase, ladder' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich fell down the stairs!

examples.text: Марина! Аркадий Борисович с лестницы упал!
examples.trans: Marina! Arkady Borisovich fell down the stairs!

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: у меня болит живот = I have a stomach ache
у меня болит живот = I have a stomach ache

examples.text: Живот у тебя, как у депутата.
examples.trans: You've got a belly like a member of parliament.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'крутить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'twist, double over'.

examples.text: Кажется, у меня просто живот скрутило.
examples.trans: It seems my stomach simply cramped up.

examples.text: Это слово «скрутить» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'twist' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?
